title: Generated Next.js apps ship BOTH App Router and Pages Router files, producing the 'Conflicting app and page' build-breaker, because nothing pins a single router
file: skyn3t/agents/architect.py:20-31 (_SYSTEM) + skyn3t/agents/code_agent.py:176,329-340 (completion scaffold-floor) + skyn3t/agents/code_agent.py:738-800 (_repair_entrypoints has no nextjs branch)
root_cause: Three independent gaps combine. (1) The architect LLM is the sole decider of project structure for nextjs, and its system prompt (architect.py:20-31) only says 'UI components/routes (for web apps)' with NO instruction to pick ONE Next.js router. So plan.files freely mixes app/page.tsx + app/layout.tsx AND pages/index.tsx + pages/_app.tsx + pages/api/*. nextjs is also deliberately excluded from _JSX_STACKS (architect.py:36,113), so the architect emits .tsx route files against a scaffold floor that is plain .jsx + jsconfig.json — exactly the jsconfig.json + .tsx/.ts mismatch and dead pages/api/auth dir seen in delivered apps 8cdb0431, c60c2d21, 231c8359. (2) The completion (OpenRouter) codegen path AMPLIFIES this into a guaranteed collision: code_agent.py:176 seeds files = dict(scaffold) and _planned_paths (code_agent.py:329-340) always re-appends the scaffold keys, so the App Router files app/page.jsx + app/layout.jsx are ALWAYS written to disk even when the architect planned a pure Pages Router app. App/page (route '/') + pages/index (route '/') then collide and `next build` fails with 'Conflicting app and page file'. (3) There is NO normalization anywhere that collapses to a single router: code_agent._repair_entrypoints (code_agent.py:738-800) has python_cli/react_vite/node_express branches but no nextjs branch; grep of runner.py and proof_run.py for pages/ | app/page | router | Conflicting returns zero collision handling, so proof_run greenlights the tree (and on builds whose only collision is pages/api vs app routes, next build even passes over orphaned dead code).
proposed_fix: Add a nextjs router-normalization step and pin the router at the source: (A) In code_agent._repair_entrypoints add a `if stack in ('nextjs','next')` branch (or a dedicated _normalize_nextjs_router(files)) that enforces ONE router: if any App Router route file exists (app/page.*, app/layout.*), DROP the colliding top-level Pages Router files (pages/index.*, pages/_app.*, pages/_document.*) and keep pages/api/* only when no app/api/* exists; mirror in reverse if the delivery is predominantly Pages Router. This guarantees a buildable tree regardless of what the architect/LLM emits. (B) In architect.py add a nextjs directive mirroring the _JSX_STACKS block (architect.py:94-96): when stack in ('nextjs','next'), append 'IMPORTANT: use the App Router ONLY — put routes under app/ (app/page.jsx, app/layout.jsx, app/api/<route>/route.js); NEVER create a pages/ directory or any Pages Router files (no pages/index, pages/_app, pages/api). Use plain .jsx/.js to match the scaffold (no tsconfig).' and run a _jsx_only-style pass for nextjs so plan files are .jsx, eliminating the jsconfig.json+.tsx mismatch too. (C) Add the same single-router instruction to code_agent._agentic_prompt (code_agent.py:342-376) for the agentic path. The normalization in (A) is the load-bearing fix; (B)/(C) reduce churn.

title: Next.js architect plans emit .tsx/.ts + no tsconfig against a plain-.jsx scaffold floor, leaving orphaned TypeScript modules and a jsconfig/typescript mismatch
root_cause: The offline/scaffold nextjs floor is intentionally plain JSX with jsconfig.json and no typescript dep (_scaffold.py:771-873, package.json declares only next/react/react-dom). But _JSX_STACKS (architect.py:36) only normalizes react/react_vite/vite, so for nextjs the architect emits .tsx/.ts files and frequently a tsconfig-less TS setup. Result: the scaffold's app/page.jsx renders the route while the architect's .tsx component modules become ORPHANS that next build never compiles (homarr 231c8359: 9 generated .tsx/.ts files under components/hooks/lib/src/store/types are unreachable; next build emitted only '/' and '/_not-found'). A 'go/100' thus certifies a thin .jsx shell over unbuilt .tsx code.
proposed_fix: Add 'nextjs'/'next' to _JSX_STACKS (architect.py:36) so _jsx_only (architect.py:39-55) rewrites .tsx->.jsx / .ts->.js and drops tsconfig for the nextjs plan, OR — if TS is desired — change the nextjs scaffold (_scaffold.py:_nextjs) to ship tsconfig.json + a `typescript`/`@types` dependency and .tsx entry files so plan and floor agree. Pick one TS posture and make scaffold + architect agree; the cheap fix is adding nextjs to _JSX_STACKS to match the existing plain-JSX scaffold.

Evidence pack STRUCTURAL RED FLAGS: all three nextjs apps show 'jsconfig.json + .tsx/.ts mix' and homarr's 9 orphaned .tsx modules.
repro: Static, code-evident; confirmed in delivered app /Users/stephenchoate/Documents/Projects/a-dashboad-like-homarr-but-newer (jsconfig.json present, .tsx files never built by next build).

title: package.json dependency versions are LLM-authored and never validated/resolved against the npm registry
root_cause: Dependency version strings come from one of two places, neither of which validates them. (1) The scaffold ships a CORRECT pinned package.json (e.g. _scaffold.py:288,601,793 etc.), but in the completion/agentic codegen backends the LLM rewrites/extends package.json wholesale with whatever versions it hallucinates. (2) reconcile_npm_deps (proof_run.py:504-552) only ADDS imported-but-undeclared package NAMES, pinning each to _KNOWN_NPM_VERSIONS or the string "latest" (proof_run.py:550) — it never inspects, validates, or corrects the version strings the LLM already wrote. There is no `npm view`/registry resolution, no peer-compat check, and no normalization of bogus pins anywhere in the pipeline (grep for ETARGET/E404/npm view/registry returns nothing). Result: hallucinated combos like @react-three/fiber@8.15.21 + @react-three/drei@9.112.0 (peer mismatch), openscad-openjscad@0.0.18 (likely nonexistent), and node-mocks-http@"latest" (a test-only dep parked in `dependencies`) ship verbatim. The delivered-evidence is partly genuine but the stated ROOT CAUSE is mislocated and the one actually-breaking item is already handled in the current code.

What's true: the delivered package.json files do contain the claimed strings. choates (Projects/build-a-air-condition-website-called-choates-hea/package.json) has the key " slick-carousel" with a literal leading space plus several "latest" pins; 3d-mod (Projects/i-want-to-build-a-web-app-that-can-create-3d-mod/package.json) has node-mocks-http:"latest" in prod deps and @react-three/fiber 8.15.21 + @react-three/drei 9.112.0.

1. The genuinely build-breaking element (the leading-space EINVALIDPACKAGENAME key) is ALREADY caught by an existing proof gate, not by reconcile_npm_deps. skyn3t/studio/proof_run.py:463 `_invalid_npm_package_names` was extended (working-tree change, git diff @475) with `or re.search(r"\s", name)` whose comment literally cites `" slick-carousel"` and EINVALIDPACKAGENAME. proof_run.py:623-629 sets passed=False when any invalid name is found. I ran it: `_project_invalid_npm_package_names()` returns [' slick-carousel'] for the choates app (and [] for 3d-mod), so the build now fails proof on exactly this. Net: the reproduced break (whitespace dep key) is already detected and gated; the rest ('latest' pins, peer combos) are residual quality nits, not a structural break, and the stated root cause is superficial/mislocated. real=false, low residual severity.

GROUNDED CORE BUG (real, high-impact): The delivered app build-a-air-condition-website-called-choates-hea/package.json has dependency key ' slick-carousel' with a literal leading space (confirmed via json.load: repr(k)==' slick-carousel'). npm rejects this with EINVALIDPACKAGENAME, which aborts the ENTIRE install (not just that pkg), so the app cannot run. 'latest' is a valid npm dist-tag that installs fine, and reconcile_npm_deps DELIBERATELY writes 'latest' itself (proof_run.py:550: deps[m]=_KNOWN_NPM_VERSIONS.get(m,"latest"); comment at :441). The proposed-fix step "replace 'latest' with a concrete pinned version" therefore contradicts existing intentional design and would REGRESS valid builds (risk of picking nonexistent/conflicting versions). This part should be dropped.
2. The 3d-mod "peer-incompatible fiber/drei pair" claim is wrong: @react-three/drei@9.x is the matched generation for @react-three/fiber@8.x (drei 10 needs fiber 9). drei 9.112.0 + fiber 8.15.21 is the CORRECT pairing, not a mismatch. node-mocks-http@'latest' in prod deps is cosmetic (installs fine, no runtime break). openscad-openjscad@0.0.18 install failure was asserted, not reproduced.
3. Whitespace detection ALREADY partly exists: _invalid_npm_package_names (proof_run.py:463-485) flags whitespace keys (working-tree change added re.search(r"\s", name) with a comment naming " slick-carousel"), setting passed=False and triggering _fix_loop (runner.py:1490). It records/repairs-via-loop but does not sanitize at delivery — so the underlying defect is genuine.

NET: the whitespace-key defect is a real, reproduced, install-blocking bug worth fixing, and the proposed-fix's strip()/reject-empty-names sanitizer in reconcile_npm_deps is sound and would actually repair the delivered package.json (better than the record-only gate). But the finding bundles three non-bugs ('latest', fiber/drei, prod test dep), and the 'latest'-replacement portion of the fix would break valid cases. Implement only the whitespace/empty-name sanitization; do not touch 'latest' or attempt version "incompatibility" rewrites.

title: Final numeric score is decoupled from verdict, producing misleading score=100 + verdict=no_go (and a 50.0 floor cluster)
root_cause: final_score = _honest_score(0.6*reviewer + 0.4*proof.score, proof.passed) is computed independently of the boolean go/no_go conjunction (runner.py:1630). A delivered build that fails the AND of gates (e.g. reviewer brief-aware no_go) can still carry a perfect blended score, and the no_go path frequently lands at the default/floor 50.0. The persisted `score` column is therefore not a reliable delivery-quality signal on its own.
evidence: DB builds: 3a62252e (no_go, score 100.0), 651848aa (no_go, score 100.0); no_go cluster pinned at 50.0 (02b5bb2a, 89afc0a5, cd6a63b4, 5777683c, 997450c4, 1d040d29). _honest_score only halves when proof failed (runner.py:2001-2007), not when the verdict conjunction fails for other reasons.
repro: sqlite3 data/skyn3t.db 'select bid,verdict,score from builds order by created_at desc' → rows with verdict=no_go and score=100.0.
proposed_fix: Clamp displayed/persisted score to a no_go ceiling (e.g. cap at <60, the reviewer GO_THRESHOLD) whenever the final verdict is no_go, so score and verdict never visibly contradict; or surface them as one combined delivery grade.

verdicts.reasoning: Code matches the report exactly. runner.py:1562-1564 computes final_score = _honest_score(round(0.6*reviewer_score + 0.4*proof.score,2), proof.passed) independently of the verdict. The verdict conjunction (runner.py:1630-1636) ANDs in proof.passed, delivered_nonempty, substantive, has_entry, intent_ok, critic_gate, not scaffold_stub, not code_degraded. _honest_score (runner.py:2001-2007) only halves the blend when proof_passed is False. Score dampening for gate failures exists ONLY for code_degraded (1640-1642) and intent (1656-1658), each additionally gated on proof.passed; the scaffold_stub/has_entry/substantive/critic gates flip the verdict but never reduce the score. Manifest inspection shows 3a62252e and 651848aa were flipped to no_go solely by scaffold_stub_gate while intent=100.0 and proof passed — the exact decoupling path. A 50.0 cluster (02b5bb2a, 89afc0a5, cd6a63b4, 5777683c, 997450c4, 1d040d29, etc.) corresponds to proof-failed halving. Genuine signal-quality bug: persisted score contradicts verdict and, per the in-code comments at 1637-1640/2005, the learning loop grades on score, so a scaffold-stub build escapes the dampening those comments intend. Medium severity — no crash, but corrupts the learning/delivery signal. Not one of the already-fixed items.

Confirmed and reproduced. DB (data/skyn3t.db) has no_go builds with score=100.0: 3a62252e, 651848aa, 062853ef. For the two clean cases the manifest.extra shows scaffold_stub_gate fired with proof.passed=true and intent heuristic=100, so runner.py:1562-1565 computes final_score=_honest_score(0.6*100+0.4*100, True)=100, while the verdict AND at runner.py:1630-1636 flipped to no_go on `not scaffold_stub`. The remaining verdict-flipping gates — scaffold_stub (1607-1610), substantive (1579), has_entry (1573), critic_gate (1629), and the liveness hard-gate (659-662) — flip the verdict without touching the score, so no_go+100 is structurally possible and observed. The decoupling also reaches the learning loop: lesson_quality=final_score/100 (1682) uses the undampened score. title: go/100 can certify an app whose generated bulk is unreachable dead code
root_cause: proof_run's _unwired_components and import checks operate on reachable imports from the entrypoint. When codegen emits a self-contained entrypoint plus many orphaned generated modules (and even an empty route dir), `next build` compiles only the reachable entrypoint and proof passes; the orphaned .tsx/.ts files are never imported, built, or exercised, so a 'go' certifies a thin shell over unbuilt generated code.
evidence: Delivered build 231c8359 (homarr, go/100): app/page.jsx imports only react + ./globals.css; the 9 generated components/hooks/lib/src/store/types .tsx/.ts modules are never imported; pages/api/auth is an empty directory. `npx next build` emitted only Route ○ / and ○ /_not-found — confirming the rest is unreachable.
repro: npx next build in /Users/stephenchoate/Documents/Projects/a-dashboad-like-homarr-but-newer → only '/' and '/_not-found' routes; grep shows components/* never imported.
proposed_fix: Add an orphaned-file check to proof_run: flag generated source files (excluding tests/config) that are never reachable from the entrypoint import graph as advisory gaps, and dampen score when a large fraction of generated bytes is unreachable, so 'go' reflects what was actually built.

verdicts.reasoning: Grounded in code + DB. proof_run.py HAS an orphaned-entry guard (_unwired_components, :287-308, called :674-681) that flags "entry reaches none of the generated components." It would have fired on this build, but it is short-circuited at proof_run.py:290-291 by _has_path_aliases (:249-260), which returns True whenever a tsconfig/jsconfig contains "paths". The delivered app /Users/stephenchoate/Documents/Projects/a-dashboad-like-homarr-but-newer/jsconfig.json has a full "paths" block, so the check returns None and never runs. _reachable_files (:263-284) also only follows relative imports, so alias reachability is untraceable. DB confirms build 231c8359a635 scored 100.0 verdict 'go' (sqlite3 data/skyn3t.db). app/ contains only layout.jsx/page.jsx/globals.css; grep '@/' app/ is empty; page+layout import only react + ./globals.css, so the 9 generated modules (components/*, hooks/*, lib/*, store/*, types/*, src/config.js) and empty pages/api/auth are unreachable dead code the 'go' counts as delivered. So the finding's conclusion (go/100 certifies an app whose generated bulk is unreachable) is real and reproduced. Caveats lowering severity/confidence: (1) the entry is NOT a stub — app/page.jsx is a working ~120-line dashboard, so the user gets a functional app, contradicting the report's 'thin shell' phrasing; (2) the report's root-cause is imprecise — it claims no orphan check exists, when one exists but is disabled by the path-alias short-circuit, so the proposed fix ('add an orphaned-file check') duplicates existing code rather than fixing _has_path_aliases; (3) I did not run npx next build, so the report's claimed route output is unverified, though the dead-code conclusion holds from import-graph inspection.

Reproduced on delivered build (/Users/stephenchoate/Documents/Projects/a-dashboad-like-homarr-but-newer, manifest verdict=go score=100). 1683 lines of substantive generated modules (components/DashboardLayout.tsx, DragDropContext.tsx, Widget.tsx, hooks/useWidgets.ts+useServices.ts, store/widgetsStore.ts, lib/api.ts, lib/auth.ts, types/widgets.ts) are never imported by anything in app/ (grep: 'NONE in app/'), and pages/api/auth is an empty dir. So go/100 does certify an app carrying large unreachable generated bulk — the observation is grounded.

However the stated root cause is imprecise/overstated on two counts: (1) The 'thin shell over unbuilt generated code' framing is wrong — app/page.jsx is a complete, working ~150-line dashboard (search, filter, stats, service grid). The certified app genuinely boots/builds/runs; the real defect is that the requested drag-drop widget system shipped as DEAD code, not that the entry is a stub. (2) The finder missed the actual mechanism. proof_run already HAS the check for this — _unwired_components (skyn3t/studio/proof_run.py:287-308) flags 'entry reaches none of the generated components.' I ran it on the app: it returns None because (a) _has_path_aliases is True (jsconfig.json declares 'paths') so line 290-291 short-circuits before computing reachability, and (b) _ENTRY_NAMES (line 244-246) omits Next.js app-router entries page.jsx/layout.jsx, so _reachable_files returns an empty set anyway. AND liveness `skipped: no live preview` — i.e. they went go/100 with zero runtime verification.

Verdict: real gap, correctly attributed to the build-as-runtime-proxy design of proof_run. Severity medium rather than high: a partial render-checking pipeline (liveness/visual) already exists and would catch many blank-page cases when vision+Playwright are wired; the precise unclosed hole is that the served check is HTTP-status-only and non-gating-by-default, which the proposed fix should harden (preferably in the existing liveness path) rather than duplicating a server inside proof_run.

The finder's narrow file-level claim is true: `skyn3t/studio/proof_run.py::_run_node_build` (proof_run.py:1021-1090) only runs `npm install` + `npm run build`/`typecheck` and never boots/serves the app. But the finder grepped ONLY proof_run.py and concluded the whole pipeline lacks a runtime-execution gate — that conclusion is wrong. - runner.py:1669 invokes `_run_liveness` for web stacks whenever `liveness_check_enabled` (default True, getattr fallback at line 1669).
- `_run_liveness` (runner.py:626-672) -> `liveness_self_improve` (liveness.py:232) -> `AppRunner.start` (app_runner.py:405) actually SERVES the delivered app via `subprocess.Popen` of `npm run dev`/start or `python -m http.server` (app_runner.py:313, 435), waits for the port to answer (app_runner.py:472-481, _port_answers:513), then `check_liveness` (liveness.py:171-189) hits every enumerated/crawled route over HTTP with ok=200<=status<400, and `_judge_page` captures a Playwright screenshot and vision-judges it (visual_check.py:48-66, 184-217). Dead routes dampen the score by health (runner.py:665-668) and can hard-gate to no_go.

So client-side dead/blank routes do affect the outcome by default (score dampening + optional vision judgement), contradicting the finder's "never fail the proof / shipped apps silently broken" premise.

(2) "zero uncaught console errors" is over-strict (benign React dev warnings, favicon/sourcemap 404s). (3) Requiring a successful prod-server boot would false-fail apps that legitimately need env/DB/keys in the sandbox — app_runner already treats these as SOFT failures with a missing-secrets hint (app_runner.py:451-460), not a hard fail. Residual nuance (why severity=low not none): liveness's HARD verdict gate `liveness_gates_verdict` is opt-in (default False, runner.py:670), so by default a runtime-crashing route only dampens the score rather than forcing no_go. That is a deliberate design choice, not the total absence the finder claims. Net: genuine file-level observation, but the asserted impact is refuted and the proposed fix would break valid SPA/env-dependent cases -> real=false.

NET: real design gap exists (request-time execution is opt-in, not hard-gating) but it is a deliberate tradeoff with existing default liveness coverage, and the offered remedies are unsound (regressions) or redundant. Marking real=false, severity low.

title: Test-first acceptance suite is behavior-free: even when executed it only asserts file-presence and that each criterion string has >=2 words
root_cause: TestAuthorAgent always writes a Python file `tests/test_acceptance_{slug}.py` regardless of stack (test_author.py:174 — even for react/nextjs/astro/remix). Because it is a .py file under tests/, _has_python_tests(pdir) returns True, so for a web build _run_generated_tests does NOT early-skip — it actually runs pytest. But render_test_file (test_author.py:66-136) emits only three structural assertions: test_project_has_source_content (a non-empty source file exists), test_project_has_entrypoint (a filename in a hardcoded set exists), and a parametrized test_acceptance_criterion_documented whose ENTIRE assertion is `assert isinstance(criterion, str) and len(criterion.split()) >= 2` (test_author.py:135) — i.e. it verifies the acceptance-criterion TEXT has at least two words, not that the app satisfies it. For a web app this pytest never installs npm, never renders a component, never hits a route. So when test-first is enabled, a web build can report detail['tests']='passed' (proof_run.py:689) with literally zero behavioral verification of the delivered application — green that certifies 'the criterion strings I wrote are >=2 words long'.

title: Singleton CodeAgent.metadata['degraded'] leaks across builds, producing false no_go + halved score on subsequent clean builds
root_cause: CodeAgent is a single long-lived instance registered once per process (cli/main.py build_agents/_assemble_spine). Its `self.metadata` dict is created once in the base Agent __init__ (skyn3t/core/agent.py:92) and is NEVER reset per task. BaseAgent._run_locked (agent.py:141-158) only clears the LLM route capture, not self.metadata. The agentic code path writes self.metadata['degraded']=True / 'degraded_reason' (code_agent.py:256-257) when a build under-delivers, and execute() reads those SAME keys back to build its output dict (code_agent.py:310-312). Because the keys persist on the shared instance, the NEXT build whose code stage succeeds cleanly (and never enters the degraded branch) still reads the stale self.metadata['degraded']==True at line 310 and emits out['degraded']=True with the PRIOR build's reason. The runner then sets `code_degraded = prior['code']['degraded']` (runner.py:1618-1621) which forces verdict to no_go (the final go-gate ANDs `and not code_degraded`, runner.py:1632-1635) and halves final_score (runner.py:1640-1641). One degraded agentic build thus 'sticks' and false-no_go's every subsequent monolithic build in the same server session until restart — consistent with the DB's no_go-at-50.0 clusters. _run_lock serializes concurrent runs but does nothing about cross-run carryover.
evidence: Reproduced: `a=CodeAgent(...); a.metadata['degraded']=True; a.metadata['degraded_reason']='build N agentic under-delivered'` then re-running the exact output-build lines 310-312 for a clean build N+1 yields `out.degraded = True -> build N agentic under-delivered`. agent.py:92 `self.metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}` (init once); execute() (code_agent.py:151) has no `self.metadata.clear()` at entry; gate at runner.py:1618-1621 `code_degraded = code_backend != 'stub' and bool((prior.get('code') or {}).get('degraded'))`.
proposed_fix: Stop using shared instance state for per-run signals. At the top of CodeAgent.execute() snapshot into a local dict (`meta = {'backend': self.llm.backend}`) and use `meta` for degraded/agentic/prose_rejected, returning out['degraded'] from `meta`, never from self.metadata. Minimal alternative: reset the per-run keys at execute() entry, e.g. `self.metadata.pop('degraded', None); self.metadata.pop('degraded_reason', None); self.metadata.pop('prose_rejected', None)`. Best: have BaseAgent._run_locked reset a per-run scratch namespace (e.g. clear self.metadata back to its initialized keys) before calling execute().
repro: python3 -c reproduction above; statically: code_agent.py:256/310 read+write self.metadata, agent.py:92 inits once and _run_locked (agent.py:141) never resets it.

Root cause is accurate and grounded in real code. self.metadata is initialized once (skyn3t/core/agent.py:92) and BaseAgent._run_locked (agent.py:141-158) resets only the LLM route capture, never self.metadata. Confirmed the leak is genuine and the proposed fix is sound, with two important scope caveats.

INSTANCE MODEL (singleton confirmed): build_agents() builds agents once (skyn3t/cli/main.py:224) and registers them on a long-lived Orchestrator held in the spine (_assemble_spine, main.py:218-241). The web server reuses one spine across builds, so the registered CodeAgent is a single long-lived instance. BaseAgent.__init__ creates self.metadata once (skyn3t/core/agent.py:92) and _run_locked (agent.py:141-203) only resets the LLM route capture (begin_run_capture/routes.clear at 153-158) — it never touches self.metadata before or after execute(). No reset anywhere.

LEAK PATH (confirmed): In the agentic branch, degraded is only set inside the under-delivery branch (code_agent.py:256-257). A clean agentic build (under_delivered=False, agentic_ok=True) takes files=disk at 265 and never enters 238/256, so a prior build's self.metadata['degraded'] survives. The output tail unconditionally reads it back (code_agent.py:310-312), so build N+1 emits out['degraded']=True with build N's reason. Reproduced exactly: feeding the 256/310 tail logic with a shared dict, a clean build N+1 inherits 'degraded': True, 'degraded_reason': 'build N agentic under-delivered'.

PROPOSED FIX SOUNDNESS: All three variants resolve it without regressing valid builds — degraded is recomputed every run, so popping the keys at execute() entry or snapshotting into a local meta dict is safe. The 'minimal' (pop degraded/degraded_reason/prose_rejected at entry) and 'local meta dict' options are clean. The 'best' variant (fully clear metadata in _run_locked) would also wipe metadata['backend'] set in initialize() (149), but grep shows nothing reads metadata['backend'] back (output uses self.llm.backend at 306), so even that doesn't regress — though the local-dict/pop options are strictly safer.

The OpenRouter completion path (275-296) never sets degraded, so in a pure-completion session — the current default per memory — no degraded is ever produced and there is NO leak. The bug is dormant under the present config and active only when the agentic CLI backend is used. (2) It does NOT cause shipped apps to fail to run — the delivered app is the clean agentic app; the harm is a false no_go verdict + halved score that also poisons the learning loop (which grades on score). Severity is high for verdict/learning correctness when the agentic backend is active, not for app runnability. Distinct from the 3 already-fixed items.

title: reconcile_orphaned_builds blanket-marks ALL 'running' rows interrupted, clobbering live builds owned by a concurrent process sharing skyn3t.db
root_cause: reconcile_orphaned_builds (store.py:185-197) runs at startup and executes `UPDATE BuildRow SET status='interrupted' WHERE status=='running'` with NO scoping to the current process/PID/host. The docstring assumes a single server and that 'a build can't survive a server restart', but data/skyn3t.db is a shared file DB and the project runs multiple services (dashboard + CLI builds). If a second process starts (or the dashboard is restarted — the documented restart-after-settings-change workflow) WHILE another process still has an in-flight build persisted as status='running' (set at runner.py:1244/1255 before the long stage loop), the startup reconcile overwrites that live build's row to status='interrupted'. The owning process later writes its real verdict (runner.py:1710/1731/2145), but if it was killed or races, the row is left interrupted/null-verdict. This matches the DB's interrupted/null-verdict rows (e.g. 1da9cf72 regression-check, status=interrupted, verdict null).
evidence: store.py:191-196 `update(BuildRow).where(BuildRow.status == 'running').values(status='interrupted')` — unconditional on owner; runner.py:1244 `manifest.status = 'running'` persisted at 1255 at build start, real status only written post-loop at 1710/1731/2145.
proposed_fix: Scope orphan reconciliation to the current process: stamp each running BuildRow with a process token (PID+boot-time or a server-session UUID minted at startup) when status is set to 'running', and reconcile only rows whose token != the current session token AND whose token's process is no longer alive. At minimum add a heartbeat/updated_at and only interrupt rows whose updated_at is older than a threshold, so a freshly-started concurrent build is not clobbered.
repro: static: store.py:185-197; tie-in: sqlite3 data/skyn3t.db 'select build_id,slug,status,verdict from builds where status="interrupted"' shows 1da9cf72 with null verdict.

verdicts.reasoning:
Code claim is accurate. skyn3t/memory/store.py:185-197 `reconcile_orphaned_builds` runs exactly `update(BuildRow).where(BuildRow.status == "running").values(status="interrupted")` with NO process/PID/host/session scoping — confirmed verbatim. It is invoked unconditionally on web-server startup (skyn3t/web/app.py:130-139, `@app.on_event("startup")`). The runner sets `manifest.status = "running"` and persists it immediately at build start (skyn3t/studio/runner.py:1244 + 1255 `_save_build`), and only writes the real terminal status post-loop (runner.py:1673/1710/1731 and final save at 2145) — the report's line numbers match within 1-2 lines.

Concurrency premise is real: a SECOND long-lived process exists. The CLI build path `skyn3t studio_build` -> `_run_build` (skyn3t/cli/main.py:566) -> `StudioRunner.start` uses the same MemoryStore over the same single-file SQLite DB (settings.py:224 `sqlite+aiosqlite:///{data_dir}/skyn3t.db`) and does NOT call reconcile. So if a CLI build is in flight (row status='running') while the web dashboard is (re)started — the documented restart-after-settings-change workflow — the startup reconcile blanket-flips that live build's row to 'interrupted'. Mechanism confirmed.

Caveats lowering confidence/severity: (1) The clobber is largely self-healing — a CLI build that completes normally overwrites its row back to the real terminal status at runner.py:1673/1710/1731/2145, so the wrong 'interrupted' is only transient (during the build window the slug looks free / UI shows a phantom). Persistent damage requires the concurrent build to also be killed, in which case 'interrupted' is arguably the correct outcome anyway. (2) The DB 'evidence' is circumstantial, not a reproduction: I confirmed 3 interrupted rows exist (`sqlite3 data/skyn3t.db`), including 1da9cf72a8...4134 'regression-check' status=interrupted — but these are equally explained by the intended single-process orphan reconcile (web server killed mid-build) and do NOT prove a cross-process clobber happened. Also the report says "null verdict"; the verdict column is `VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL` and the actual stored value is empty string '', not NULL — a minor inaccuracy. So: genuine logic gap (no owner scoping on a shared DB with multiple build entry points), but narrower real-world impact than "clobbering live builds" implies, and the cited row does not actually substantiate that it occurred.

The stated mechanism is accurately grounded in real code, not a symptom, and has no existing mitigation — so the root cause is correct. But the practical blast radius is smaller than the "medium" claim, and the cited DB evidence does not actually confirm the clobber-live-build scenario.

GROUNDING (confirmed):
- skyn3t/memory/store.py:191-196 — `update(BuildRow).where(BuildRow.status == "running").values(status="interrupted")` is a blanket, unscoped UPDATE: no PID, no session token, no host, no updated_at filter. Confirmed schema (`sqlite3 data/skyn3t.db ".schema builds"`) has only `created_at` — there is NO updated_at/heartbeat column, and `grep pid|session|token|heartbeat|updated_at skyn3t/memory/store.py` returns nothing, so no scoping exists anywhere.
- It is invoked ONLY at web-server startup: skyn3t/web/app.py:129-139 (`_reconcile_orphans` on_event("startup")).
- A CLI build is a genuinely SEPARATE process on the SAME DB: skyn3t/cli/main.py:566 `_run_build` -> `_assemble_spine` builds its own `MemoryStore(settings)` (cli/main.py:210-213) pointing at data/skyn3t.db, and runs `StudioRunner.start` end-to-end in that process. runner.py:1244 `manifest.status = "running"` is persisted immediately at runner.py:1255 `await self._save_build(manifest)`, before the long stage loop. The real verdict is written post-loop at runner.py:1710/1731/2145.
- So the docstring's assumption (store.py:186-188 "A build can't survive a server restart") is FALSE for the separate CLI build process. A web restart (the user's documented restart-after-settings-change workflow) during an in-flight `skyn3t studio build` will mark that live build's row interrupted. That much is a real, unmitigated design flaw.

WHY SEVERITY IS LOWER THAN CLAIMED:
- Self-healing: the owning CLI process overwrites the wrongly-set 'interrupted' with its true verdict at runner.py:1710/1731/2145 (save_build at store.py:143 is an upsert by build_id). So PERSISTENT corruption only occurs if the build ALSO dies — which is exactly the legitimate orphan case the function is designed to handle. The lasting damage is therefore indistinguishable from a true orphan.
- The cited "evidence" is circumstantial, not a repro: `select * from builds where status='interrupted'` returns 3 rows (abfe00ee.., 2bd0a68d.., 1da9cf72..), all with empty verdict. These are equally consistent with genuinely orphaned builds (server killed mid-build). Nothing distinguishes a clobbered-live-build from a real orphan, so they do not prove the bug fired. (Note: verdict is VARCHAR NOT NULL, so it's empty-string "", not NULL as the finding states.)
- Real-world harm reduces to a transient window of wrong dashboard/slug-busy state during a long (~20-30 min per codegen-timeout memory) concurrent CLI build that is restarted-over, which self-corrects on completion. Genuine but low blast radius.

NET: root cause is real and unmitigated; rate real=true but severity low, not medium.

The code description is accurate: reconcile_orphaned_builds (store.py:191-196) does an unconditional UPDATE...WHERE status=='running' with no owner scoping, runs at web-server startup (app.py:130-139), and runner persists 'running' at build start (runner.py:1244/1255). The race is theoretically possible if a second process runs a build while the web server restarts. BUT impact does not reach "shipped app doesn't run": (1) reconcile only mutates the DB `status` bookkeeping column — it never kills a process or touches the delivered files under Projects/; (2) save_build (store.py:143-153) is an upsert keyed on build_id, so the owning process overwrites the clobbered `interrupted` row with the real verdict at runner.py:1710/1731/2145 — the clobber self-heals unless the owner is also killed, in which case `interrupted` is the correct result; (3) the cleanup "active slug" protection that guards live builds uses in-memory state.builds (routes.py:1208-1209/1221-1222), NOT the DB status, so a clobbered row cannot expose a live build to deletion. The cited evidence (1da9cf72 'regression-check', null verdict) is a test/regression slug, far more plausibly a genuine orphan (the intended cleanup case) than a concurrency clobber — it is not a reproduction. Net: a real-but-narrow status-field race with no functional/app-runnability impact; cosmetic. The session-token fix would work; the cheaper heartbeat-threshold variant has its own regressions (young orphans linger, old stalled-but-alive builds still clobbered).
